place: pantropical, Amazonia, Central Africa, Southeast Asia
data: Landsat Analysis Ready Data within intact tropical forest masks, with Global Forest Change and Tropical Moist Forest for calibration and comparison
method: Normalized Burn Ratio time series with forest based local standardization, a statistical change indicator, cloud tolerant masking and spatial and temporal refinement of candidate events
validation: two level validation combining spatial intersections and temporal stratification, compared with global datasets
measures: bias and root mean square error of annual deforestation estimates, values not stated
finding: A Landsat time series method estimated annual deforestation in Central Africa with lower bias and root mean square error than global datasets, most clearly in the Congo Basin.
gap_quote: These challenges are most pronounced in regions such as the Congo Basin, where observational limitations lead to uneven detection performance and reduced comparability across datasets.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kongo Central, Kasangulu territory
method: remote sensing of Landsat and Sentinel imagery with a survey of 210 households and qualitative interviews
finding: Kasangulu's miombo woodland lost 33 per cent of its area from 2000 to 2025, and charcoal production accounted for about 60 per cent of that deforestation.
gap_quote: Despite a strong awareness of forest decline, attempts to adopt improved kilns or reforestation largely fail (>80% abandonment rate) due to economic, land tenure, and technical constraints.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Indonesia, Peru
data: Landsat 5 and 7 Thematic Mapper, MODIS Vegetation Continuous Fields, Landsat VCF
method: supervised maximum likelihood classification, and MODIS VCF guided Forest Non Forest masking with k nearest neighbor classification, each followed by post classification image differencing
validation: accuracy assessment with 500 validation pixels at each study area
measures: overall accuracy by pixel counts and area proportions, values not stated
finding: Forest Non Forest masking guided by MODIS VCF gave the highest overall accuracy and best labelled change, while Landsat VCF overestimated forest cover at all three sites.
gap_quote: Landsat VCF substantially underestimates non-forested land cover and as a result overestimates forested land cover in all study areas.

data: land use change matrix in IPCC nomenclature of intact forest land, non intact forest land and other land
method: matrix approach of Bucki et al 2012 coupled to a bookkeeping carbon model, with sensitivity analysis and Monte Carlo simulation
validation: sensitivity analysis and Monte Carlo error propagation
measures: flux differences of 4.2 to 262.2 per cent of the reference emission level
finding: Released a table of land use change areas, emissions and their sensitivities for Panama's REDD+ reference emission level, 1992 to 2000, with fluxes varying 4.2 to 262.2 per cent.
gap_quote: Substantial technical challenges hinder precise and accurate estimation of forest-related emissions and removals, as well as the setting and assessment of reference levels.

area: radii of 1, 2, 10 and 30 km around each station
data: GLanCE 2001 to 2019 and GLC_FCS30D 1985 to 2022, both 30 m Landsat land cover products
method: land cover change analysis within station radii and wind sectors, homogeneity tests and machine learning anomaly detection
finding: Used GLanCE and GLC_FCS30D to measure land cover change around 62 Polish weather stations from 1985 to 2022 and tested its effect on climate records at two stations.
gap_quote: Changes in land cover around a meteorological station can influence measurement outcomes, thereby compromising the homogeneity of climatic data.

place: Amazon Basin, Jamanxim National Forest in Brazil, Amboró and Carrasco National Parks in Bolivia, Tambopata National Reserve and Bahuaja-Sonene National Park in Peru
method: land use change models informed by quantitative and qualitative analysis of conservation discourses, compared with standard land use change models
predictors: slope, population density, surrounding non forest, distance to agriculture, fires, legal threats to protected area status, payments for ecosystem services projects, REDD+ projects
finding: Models informed by conservation discourses outperformed standard models, and from 2008 to 2018 deforestation was likelier in fragments and near farms and fires, and less likely on steep slopes.
gap_quote: Standard, quantitative approaches to land-use change (LUC) modeling may omit some factors, constraining understandings of and responses to deforestation.

place: pantropical, with the Atlantic Forest, Gulf of Guinea, Thailand, Latin America, insular Southeast Asia and Madagascar named
method: geographic information systems combined with a meta analysis of ecosystem services studies, in a spatially explicit analysis of agricultural benefits against carbon and ecosystem service losses
finding: Carbon and ecosystem service losses from tropical deforestation outweighed agricultural benefits except under high value crop rents, while conversion appeared efficient in the Atlantic Forest, Gulf of Guinea and Thailand.
gap_quote: Much of this deforestation occurs with a lack of information on the spatial distribution of benefits and costs of deforestation.

place: Cameroon, north western highlands of Yaounde, Mbankolo, Febe, Carrier, Nkolbisson and Messa
data: satellite images of different periods, GPS data, field observations and surveys, topographic maps
method: geographic information system mapping from field observations, surveys and remotely sensed data
finding: Mapped poor displaced residents settling risk prone suburbs of north western Yaounde, where uncontrolled deforestation, wetland occupation and soil degradation were high.
gap_quote: Urban disorder and land use abuse marked by uncontrolled deforestation, wetland occupation and soil degradation for settlement, agriculture and commerce is high in the newly occupied zones necessitating research and measures to pre-empt future disaster in this area.

predictors: policies and institutions, agriculture, forest use and exploitation
finding: Argues that West and Central Africa lose almost 2 million hectares of rainforest a year, and that deforestation must be addressed within development policy with World Bank support.
gap_quote: If we do not begin to halt the destruction of these forests in the near future, it may become too late to preserve them.

place: Lake Tanganyika catchment, Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Tanzania
data: remote sensing estimates of vegetation cover from the ARTEMIS NDVI archive and of rainfall from the FEWS archive
method: regional soil erosion model on daily and decadal timesteps with sediment routing by sediment delivery ratio, run under land degradation and deforestation scenarios
predictors: rainfall, vegetation cover, land degradation and deforestation scenarios
finding: The model found three regions especially sensitive to erosion, one each in Burundi, Zaire and Tanzania, with near total deforestation in Burundi sending sediment into northern Lake Tanganyika.
gap_quote: Parameterisation of the model with these different spatial rainfall estimates produced quite different results in certain instances.
